meta.blog-leaseauto-belasting.html.title: Extra tax on company cars with emissions (2027): what you need to know · Lemnion
meta.blog-leaseauto-belasting.html.descr: From 1 January 2027 there is an extra tax on company cars with petrol, diesel or hybrid drive: 12% of the list price per year. What does this mean for your hotel?
blog-lease.h1: Extra tax on company cars with emissions
blog-lease.sub: From 1 January 2027 you pay extra tax on company cars with petrol, diesel or hybrid drive. What does this mean for your hotel and lease contracts?
blog-lease.intro: From 1 January 2027, an extra tax applies to company cars with emissions. Employers who offer employees a car from their own fleet or via lease, and who also use that car privately or for commuting, face a significant extra cost. For hotels this is the moment to make conscious choices about which company cars take the road in the coming years.
blog-lease.kort-li1: From 1 January 2027: extra tax on company cars with petrol, diesel or hybrid drive
blog-lease.kort-li2: Rate: 12% of the list price per year (cars up to and including 25 years old)
blog-lease.kort-li3: Cars older than 25 years: 12% of the market value
blog-lease.kort-li4: The 500-kilometre private-use limit does not apply; commuting counts as private use
blog-lease.kort-li5: Transitional arrangement for cars offered before 2027: only from 17 September 2030
blog-lease.p-wie: The measure applies to employers who offer company cars with emissions to employees who also use the car privately or for commuting. This can be a car from the company fleet or a lease car.
blog-lease.wie-li1: Hotels with their own fleet (for facilities, management or service)
blog-lease.p-wat: From 1 January 2027 you pay extra tax on company cars that are not fully emission-free, so cars with petrol, diesel or hybrid drive. The tax runs through wage tax (a so-called pseudo-final levy) and may not be charged on to your employee.
blog-lease.p-reken: A lease car with a list price of €40,000 costs 12% × €40,000 = €4,800 extra per year from 2027. For a fleet of 10 such cars this adds up to €48,000 per year extra.
blog-lease.p-overgang: For company cars with emissions that you already made available to your employees before 1 January 2027, a transitional arrangement applies: only from 17 September 2030 do you also pay the extra tax on these cars. That offers time, but is no reason to delay. Contracts you renew now or sign new will generally fall under the new rules.
blog-lease.h2-hotel: What does this mean for your hotel?
blog-lease.p-hotel: This measure accelerates the switch to electric driving. And electric driving starts with good charging infrastructure. A few things to take into account:
blog-lease.hotel-li1: Choose electric where you can: emission-free cars fall outside the new tax and become fiscally more attractive
blog-lease.hotel-li2: Charging infrastructure becomes essential: without enough charge points, electric driving becomes difficult for your team and your guests
blog-lease.hotel-li3: Avoid peak load: with smart charging and a battery, the power demand stays manageable
blog-lease.hotel-li4: Use the subsidy: SPRILA subsidises private charging infrastructure, up to €3,900 per DC charge point (SME)
blog-lease.td2: 12% of the list price per year
blog-lease.td4: 12% of the market value per year
blog-lease.p-help: Make the switch to electric driving easy and affordable. Lemnion supplies charge points and DC fast chargers, linked to battery storage and smart energy control. That way you charge employees and guests sustainably, keep peak load low and make use of the available subsidies.

blog-lease.groei-h2: The growth of electric driving: 5 and 10 years ahead
blog-lease.groei-intro: This and other tax measures accelerate the shift to electric driving. The figures underline that trend, and the fiscal course makes the growth largely irreversible for company and lease cars. What can we expect in the coming years?
blog-lease.groei-li1: Fully electric cars had a market share of 40.2% in new sales in 2025, up from 34.6% in 2024
blog-lease.groei-li2: New petrol cars fell to 13.1%; diesel to 1%
blog-lease.groei-li3: Almost 8 out of 10 new electric cars go to companies or lease, not to private buyers
blog-lease.groei-li4: Fiscal choices set the pace of the market: addition-to-salary rates and the new lease-car tax steer demand
blog-lease.groei-5p: This trend continues, especially in the company and lease segment. The 2027 measure makes cars on petrol, diesel or hybrid structurally more expensive for employers, so almost all new lease and company cars become electric. The share of electric cars in new sales is then expected to be between 60% and 70%. Because the total car fleet renews slowly, roughly a quarter of the driving fleet will be electric by then.
blog-lease.groei-10p: Even if the EU plan to sell only emission-free new cars from 2035 is adjusted, business will be almost fully electric by then. New sales could reach 80% to 90% plus electric cars, and the driving fleet 40% to 50%. Growth then focuses on the private market and the phase-out of the older fleet.
blog-lease.groei-h3-sam: What does this mean for you?
blog-lease.groei-sam: Switching to electric driving is not a question of whether, but when. The faster your company and lease fleet is electric, the lower your tax burden and the smaller the chance you fall behind. That does require charging infrastructure: at home, at work and on the road.
blog-lease.groei-bron: 2024-2025 figures: RAI Vereniging and BOVAG, via Solar & Storage Magazine (January 2026); share of company and lease cars: Autoweek. Projections for 2031 and 2036 are estimates based on these trends, not figures set by governments.
